description: The conformance corpus. Each case takes the certified base declaration, breaks exactly one fact, and records what each gate says about the result: `load` is registry validation (createProviderAdapterRegistry), `conformance` is partnerBankConformanceFindings, `schema` is spec/manifest.schema.json. Where two gates disagree, `note` says why. Read this file to see every rule and what trips it. test/conformance-cases.spec.ts runs it and fails if any conformance code goes unexercised.
mutations: `set` writes a value at a path (array of keys, because operation names contain dots) and runs before `delete`, which removes a path.

cases.title: the base declaration certifies with no findings
cases.why: The corpus is worthless if the base is not clean: every case below reads as one broken fact against a green baseline.

cases.title: no partner-bank profile at all
cases.why: Without the profile none of the bank facts exist, so the runtime has nothing to poll, classify, or reconcile from.

cases.title: a missing profile leads, and the declaration checks still run
cases.why: One run must report everything it can see; a missing profile is not a licence to stop reading the rest.

cases.title: no operations are bound
cases.why: An adapter with no commands serves nothing, and every command-level rule below would be vacuously green.

cases.title: a live command with no response envelope class
cases.why: Without a class the runtime cannot tell acceptance from rejection, and a rejection read as silence strands money in flight.

cases.title: the envelope class is declared unconfirmed
cases.why: `unconfirmed_until_live` is the honest authoring state for a provider that publishes no error sample, and certification is the licence to serve live.

cases.title: a tenant-initiated REST command with no status enquiry
cases.why: A submit whose response is lost can then only be resolved by guessing or resubmitting, and resubmitting pays twice.

cases.title: sync clearance carries its truth in band
cases.why: The exemption is earned by the egress mode: a synchronous clearance answers in the same exchange, so there is no lost response to re-read.

cases.title: a tenant-initiated command on a file-reconciling adapter
cases.why: batch_reconcile performs no per-command outbound call, so the binding promises a call the runtime cannot make.

cases.title: a tenant-initiated command on an observation-only adapter
cases.why: Same rule, the other silent egress mode: `none` sends the provider nothing at all.

cases.title: an enquiry plan an adapter has no transport to execute
cases.why: An enquiry path on an adapter that performs no REST egress is a plan the runtime can never run.

cases.title: no spelling maps to returned
cases.why: A payment ending in a return would be unclassifiable, so the payout polls forever.

cases.title: no spelling maps to received or accepted
cases.why: An acknowledgement proves the bank took the instruction, never that money moved; with no intake state every ack would have to be graded terminal or dropped.

cases.title: a spelling that trims to nothing
cases.why: Runtimes match after trimming and upper-casing, so an empty token can never match anything the bank sends.

cases.title: two spellings that normalize to one token and disagree
cases.why: Whichever the runtime matched first would decide the payment's fate, which makes classification order-dependent.

cases.title: the replay verdicts have no spelling
cases.why: The dedupe spine is reference-based, so a crash-recovery resubmission comes back as a duplicate verdict; unclassified, it reads as a fresh failure.

cases.title: no statement format is declared
cases.why: Statements are bank truth; without one, reconciliation has nothing to prove the ledger against.

cases.title: which reference comes back on a debit is unknown
cases.why: Pick the wrong one and every payout the platform instructed reads as an unexplained debit.

cases.title: a declared format with no fetch window
cases.why: The runtime cannot schedule a retrieval it has no window for.

cases.title: an end-of-day format with no paging facts
cases.why: T-1 pages over history, so how far back the archive goes and how many days one request covers are both required.

cases.title: an availability outside the vocabulary
cases.why: Every window rule branches on availability, so an unrecognized value must not slide through green.

load.throws: windows.statements.camt_053.availability must be one of T-1, today_only

cases.title: a truthy window with no availability at all
cases.why: TypeScript requires the field; a plain-JSON manifest can omit it, and an availability-less window is unschedulable.

load.throws: windows.statements.camt_053.availability must be one of T-1, today_only

cases.title: a lookback of zero days
cases.why: A window that pages back nothing cannot fetch the history it claims to.

load.throws: windows.statements.camt_053.lookbackDays must be a positive integer

cases.title: the bank's charge billing is unmodeled
cases.why: The bank's own charge debits would land as unexplained statement lines.

cases.title: post-hoc charges with no wording to recognize them by
cases.why: A post-hoc charge arrives as a bank-initiated debit recognizable only by its narrative.

cases.title: a separate tax line with no wording to recognize it by
cases.why: A separate VAT line is its own debit with its own wording.

cases.title: charges netted at instruction, tax folded in
cases.why: Nothing posts separately, so there is no debit to recognize and no narrative to declare.

cases.title: a value date offset of a day and a half
cases.why: Value dates are whole banking days; a fraction would be NaN in every comparison that follows.
cases.note: The schema encodes the D+<days> shape as a pattern; registry load does not read the offsets at all, so conformance is the gate that catches this in TypeScript.

cases.title: a T+1 offset where D+ is the vocabulary
cases.why: The template literal type stops this in TypeScript and nothing stops it in a JSON manifest.
cases.note: Same split as value-date-offset-fractional: pattern in the schema, rule in conformance, silence at registry load.

cases.title: a cutoff read on a zone that does not exist
cases.why: The cutoff is the bank's wall clock; an unreadable zone means every value date is computed somewhere else.

load.throws: windows.paymentCutoff.timeZone must be a valid IANA time zone

cases.note: JSON Schema cannot check an IANA zone name; the schema only requires a string. Both runtime gates resolve it through Intl.DateTimeFormat.

cases.title: no time zone at all
cases.why: Intl.DateTimeFormat reads an undefined zone as the host's, so absence would silently schedule the cutoff on the platform's clock.

load.throws: windows.paymentCutoff.timeZone must be a valid IANA time zone

cases.title: a cutoff time written in words
cases.why: The runtime compares HH:MM; prose compares as never.

cases.title: missing the cutoff moves value earlier, and past the forward window
cases.why: Two independent facts, reported independently on one run: a later cutoff can only push value later, and the bank must be able to honor its own after-cutoff date.

cases.title: a forward window of zero days
cases.why: The bank must be able to honor the after-cutoff value date it declares.

load.throws: windows.valueDateMaxDaysAhead must be a positive integer

cases.title: a settled resource kind with no binding mode
cases.why: Provider facts commit onto platform resources through a declared match mode; without one the bank's answer has no lawful way to land.

cases.title: a webhook plan for a resource kind the adapter does not bind
cases.why: The webhook arm of the same rule: a plan names a resource, so that resource needs a binding mode too.

cases.title: a profile with no lifecycle vocabulary
cases.why: Nothing the bank says could be classified at all.

load.throws: partner-bank profile has no lifecycle vocabulary

cases.title: an idempotency spine with no dedupe keys
cases.why: The spine is what makes a resubmission answerable; empty, every recovery is a fresh payment.

cases.title: the same dedupe key listed twice
cases.why: The list widened from a fixed triple, so it now carries the guarantees the tuple used to give for free.

cases.title: a reference length of zero
cases.why: A reference that cannot hold a character cannot carry the spine.

load.throws: idempotencySpine.instructionId.maxLength must be a positive integer

cases.title: a bank we would only hear from by callback
cases.why: Poll-first is the portable floor: a callback is at best a hint that a poll is due, never a fact to post from.

cases.title: an environment locator that names nothing
cases.why: ADL stores locators, never values, so a blank locator is the whole credential gone.

cases.title: a keychain locator missing its account
cases.why: Same rule on the other locator shape.

cases.title: a base URL that is only a path
cases.why: The runtime joins operation paths onto this; a relative base resolves against nothing.

load.throws: config.baseUrl must be an absolute URL

cases.title: a provider key with spaces and capitals
cases.why: The key is an identity used in logs, metrics, and the registry; it is lowercase and machine-shaped.

cases.title: an operation map key that does not match its binding
cases.why: The key is how the runtime looks the binding up; drift means the runtime finds nothing under the name it holds.

load.throws: operationMap key submit must match operation payout.submit

cases.note: JSON Schema has no way to require a property's key to equal a value inside it, so this one is registry-load only.

cases.title: a webhook map key that does not match its event kind
cases.why: Same reason as the operation map: the key is the lookup.

load.throws: webhookMap key wrong must match eventKind payout.settled

cases.note: Key-equals-value again: expressible in the validator, not in the schema.

cases.title: an enquiry path with nowhere to put the reference
cases.why: The runtime substitutes the declared key into the template; without the placeholder it would call the same URL for every payment.
